key_idea: The answer is simply the number of endpoints of the given segment that are not corners of the square.
sketch: Corner to opposite corner already gives two triangles (0). Corner to an interior point of a far side gives a triangle plus a quadrilateral, which needs one diagonal (1). Two non-corner endpoints give either two quadrilaterals (opposite sides) or a triangle plus a pentagon (adjacent sides); both need two extra segments, and no single segment can fix both quadrilaterals because their diagonals are never collinear. The input guarantee excludes segments lying along a side. O(1).
